concepts.def: Substance that produces H⁺ ions in solution. pH < 7.
Soluble base that produces OH⁻ ions in solution. pH > 7.
Solution with pH 7; equal H⁺ and OH⁻, e.g. pure water.
0 (strong acid) to 14 (strong alkali); each step is a 10× change in H⁺ concentration.
Strong acids (HCl) fully ionise; weak acids (CH₃COOH) only partly ionise.
Substances that change colour with pH, e.g. litmus, universal indicator.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acids, Bases & Salts — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Acids, Bases & Salts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Acids, Bases & Salts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
